prompt: Build SeatBookingBoard on top of the provided SeatRow: book and cancel single seats, count free seats, and implement findBlock(n), which reports the first row holding n adjacent free seats as "B:3-6".
explanation: The board owns a list of SeatRow objects and delegates every seat-level decision to the row, so the rules about range and double-booking live in exactly one place. findBlock is a small scanning algorithm: walk the seats in order, grow a run of free seats, reset it to zero on a taken seat, and report as soon as the run reaches the requested length -- which is what makes it return the lowest possible start. Looking a row up by label first, and returning false when there is none, keeps every public method total.
hints: Write a private helper that finds a SeatRow by its label and returns null when no row matches; every public method can start with it.
SeatRow.take and SeatRow.release already return booleans for the refused cases, so book() and cancel() are one delegation each.
For findBlock, keep an int run counter per row: run++ on a free seat, run = 0 on a taken one, and when run == n the block starts at seat - n + 1.
